subject: Allocation arbitration request — staggered GPU sizing for Skyline & Helios
messages:
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>, Rohan Mehta <rohan_mehta@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 25 May 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Allocation arbitration request — staggered GPU sizing for Skyline & Helios

Team — quick escalation. We have two near-term Dedicated commitments that overlap the same GPU pool and the current fleet plan doesn't have enough headroom to satisfy both at full committed sizing.

Summary: Skyline (HSK-3482, revenue-stage) expects 120 GPU-equivalent units across 8xA100 preemptible-style nodes starting 2026-06-15; Helios (procurement in legal) is set to sign next week for 90 GPU-equivalent units with a requested start of 2026-06-01. Both requested zonal placement in us-west-2 for latency SLAs.

Options on the table (quick take):
- Staggered ramp: Push Skyline start by 2 weeks to free early-June capacity for Helios (affects Skyline go-live).
- Fractional carve: Offer both reduced initial slices (60/50) with guaranteed linear growth over 8 weeks.
- Burst+cache: Grant Helios a limited burst window for critical jobs while Skyline keeps steady baseline; requires throttled fairshare at runtime.
- Credits: Offer Skyline credits in exchange for delayed start (commercial concession).

I attached the capacity_projection-Q2.xlsx with an overlay of the two deals and our risk bucket. Need operations input on whether we can muscle existing reserved nodes (hot-swap) or whether preemption rules will make this infeasible. Rohan — please confirm realistic carve options + whether we can reroute non-latency-critical pods to alternate zones for a 30-day window.

Ben
Senior Account Executive
Redwood Inference

Attachment: capacity_projection-Q2.xlsx (sheet: overlapping_commits)
From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>, Rohan Mehta <rohan_mehta@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 25 May 2026 10:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Allocation arbitration request — staggered GPU sizing for Skyline & Helios

Ben — thanks for the heads up. I reviewed the projection and we have two constraints: 1) the us-west-2 reserved pool is 220 GPU equivalent for the week of 6/1; 2) 40% of that pool is pinned by a multi-month Dedicated customer (non-preemptible). Practically, we can absorb Helios at full ask only if Skyline accepts either the staggered ramp or a partial initial carve.

Operational comments for Rohan: if we enable zone failover and allow Skyline to run a cold-cache in us-east-1 for the first two weeks, we preserve Skyline's SLA for most traffic and free up ~30 GPU units in us-west-2. That requires a temporary routing policy & fallthrough model swap. Does that look feasible?

Vanessa
Director, Customer Success
Redwood Inference
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Amit Shah <amit@skyline.ai>, Erin Chu <erin@helios.ai>
Cc: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 25 May 2026 11:27:00 -0700
Subject: Proposed mutual action plan & temporary sizing (Skyline / Helios)

Amit / Erin — looping you both to propose a short mutual action plan so we can avoid a hard capacity conflict. Short version: we can meet both of your needs with a two-week stagger + a small initial carve for both parties while we stabilize the fleet. Full details attached (mutual_action_plan-Skyline-Helios.pdf).

Proposal (concise):
- Helios: start 2026-06-01 with guaranteed 90 GPU-equivalent units for 30 days.
- Skyline: accept a soft start on 2026-06-15 with guaranteed 120 GPU-equivalent units but with option to begin in us-east-1 for non-latency-critical batch workloads for first 14 days. Redwood will provide a routing policy to route <30% of Skyline traffic to us-east-1 to protect latency-sensitive requests.
- Commercial: Redwood offers Skyline a $15k credit if they accept a 14-day soft start shift.
- Escalation: If either party experiences >20% SLA degradation, Redwood will enact a pre-defined remediation playbook (see link).

We want to finalize by EOD Tuesday so Ops can commit the carve. Please confirm whether the timeline/commercials are acceptable. If you'd prefer a different approach (proportional slices, burst windows), say so and we'll workshop.

Thanks,
Ben

Attachment: mutual_action_plan-Skyline-Helios.pdf
From: Amit Shah <amit@skyline.ai>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Cc: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 25 May 2026 13:41:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Proposed mutual action plan & temporary sizing (Skyline / Helios)

Ben — appreciate the clear plan. We're willing to accept a soft start to enable Helios' earlier ramp, but two asks: 1) we need a guaranteed 80 GPU baseline in us-west-2 for p95 interactive latency; 2) the credit looks reasonable but we'd prefer a sliding credit that scales with any days of reduced throughput (ties to our SLA hit metric).

Quick questions:
- Can Redwood provide a per-route token/latency dashboard for the two-week soft-start window so we can monitor p95?
- Procurement: my finance team wants the credit language in an amendment to the MSA rather than a separate one-off.

If you confirm the 80 GPU baseline and the dashboard, I'll sign off and accept the 14-day shift.

Best,
Amit
Head of Infrastructure
Skyline AI

From: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>, Rohan Mehta <rohan_mehta@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 26 May 2026 09:08:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Proposed mutual action plan & temporary sizing (Skyline / Helios)

Thanks, Ben and Amit — good progress. Quick operational notes and decision guidance:

1) Baseline guarantee: We can commit to an 80 GPU baseline in us-west-2 for Skyline during the 14-day soft-start, provided we enforce the following routing QoS: p95-critical routes pinned to the us-west-2 pool and batch routes tagged for us-east-1. Vanessa, please confirm we can create the routing rule and token-level isolate by 5/28.

2) Dashboard: We have a per-route telemetry view (Console > Routes > Skyline HSK-3482) that will show p50/p95 token latency + token count. I'll share a link for dashboard access to Amit's team.

3) Commercials & amendment: Ben, legal will need an explicit amendment draft. For timeline sensitivity, we'll provision the amendment with a one-line credit table referencing HubSpot deal HSK-3482 and sign it as an addendum (no MSA rewrite).

4) Preemption & runbook: Rohan — if we provision the carve, confirm the preemption window and the auto-fallback model variant. We must ensure Helios cannot preempt Skyline's p95-critical tokens under the carve. Provide the runbook link in your reply.

I'll approve the staggered plan contingent on Ops confirmation; if Ops says carve impossible, we'll pivot to proportional carve + enhanced credits.

Sooj
VP, Accounts
Redwood Inference

Related: HubSpot HSK-3482, Doc: https://drive.redwood/reports/capacity_projection_Q2
From: Rohan Mehta <rohan_mehta@redwood.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 26 May 2026 16:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Allocation confirmation & ops commitments — Skyline/Helios carve

Soojin / team — confirmed. Ops can implement the staggered carve with the constraints below:

- We will reserve an 80 GPU baseline in us-west-2 for Skyline, pinned to p95-critical route tokens.
- We will carve 90 GPU-equivalent units for Helios starting 2026-06-01 for a 30-day guaranteed window.
- Routing policy to send up to 30% of Skyline's non-critical batch tokens to us-east-1 will be in place by 2026-06-14 02:00 UTC.
- Preemption rules: Helios workload is marked as preemptible for any extra capacity above the guaranteed 90 units; Skyline p95 token routes cannot be preempted.
- Runbook: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/INF-2317 (playbook attached to ticket).

Notes: This requires a short maintenance window (5–10 minutes) to apply token-level isolation and routing changes; we'll schedule during low-traffic hours on 6/14. Ops will also create a per-route dashboard share for Amit (link provisioned separately).

Rohan
Staff Site Reliability Engineer, Inference Operations
Redwood Inference

Attachment: runbook-INF-2317.md (ops steps)
